summary.short: Binding rules under the IT Act 2000, in force from Gazette publication, imposing due diligence, takedown and grievance duties on intermediaries, extra duties on significant social media and online real-money gaming intermediaries, labelling of synthetic content, and a Code of Ethics for digital publishers.
summary.long: The Rules, made under section 87(1) and clauses (z) and (zg) of section 87(2) of the Information Technology Act, 2000, set due diligence duties for intermediaries (rule 3), including takedown within three hours of actual knowledge, grievance handling within seven days, retention of removed information for 180 days, and technical measures and labelling for synthetically generated information (rule 3(3)). Significant social media intermediaries and online gaming intermediaries carry additional duties (rule 4), such as appointing a Chief Compliance Officer, monthly compliance reports, user declarations of synthetic content, and first-originator identification for messaging services. Online real-money games must be verified by designated online gaming self-regulatory bodies before they may be offered (rule 4A). Publishers of news and current affairs content and of online curated content must follow a Code of Ethics with age-based ratings, and are subject to a three-tier grievance and oversight structure with Ministry blocking directions (rules 13 to 16). Where an intermediary fails to observe the Rules, section 79(1) of the Act does not apply to it and it is liable for punishment under other laws (rule 7). Grievance Appellate Committees hear appeals (rule 3A).
